classification.difficultyReason: Identify the opposite side-angle pairs, calculate both supplementary possibilities, check their validity, and translate them into two labelled triangle sketches.

content.prompt: A triangle $ABC$ has $AB=3\text{ cm}$, $AC=2\text{ cm}$ and $\angle B=35^{\circ}$. Find the two possible values of $\angle C$, correct to 1 decimal place, and sketch the triangles.

inlines.text: ; both angles give a positive third angle.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\frac{\sin C}{3}&=\frac{\sin35^{\circ}}{2}\\\sin C&=\frac{3\sin35^{\circ}}{2}\\C_1&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{3\sin35^{\circ}}{2}\right)\\C_2&=180^{\circ}-C_1\\C_1+35^{\circ}&\approx94.4^{\circ}<180^{\circ}\\C_2+35^{\circ}&\approx155.6^{\circ}<180^{\circ}\end{align*}$$Both possibilities are valid because each leaves a positive third angle. Hence $\angle C\approx59.4^{\circ}$ or $120.6^{\circ}$, correct to 1 decimal place. The sketches show both possibilities.

spec.description: Two horizontally paired unshaded triangles. The left has acute angle C; the right has obtuse angle C. Both retain vertex labels A, B and C, side labels 3 and 2, and angle B labelled 35 degrees.
spec.mathematics: AB=3 cm, AC=2 cm, B=35 degrees. C is approximately 59.357550964 degrees or 120.642449036 degrees. Coordinates are derived from these unrounded angles. Independent picture units preserve the source pairing with comparable heights.
